title: A quasi-finite cover of affine n-space has dimension at most n
statement: Let $k$ be a field, an integer $n\ge0$, and $T$ a commutative $k$-algebra of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Suppose there is a $k$-algebra homomorphism $k[t_1,\dots,t_n]\to T$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] which is quasi-finite: it is of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime of $T$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. Then the Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is at most $n$ (including the empty spectrum, whose dimension is $-\infty$).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00QG (lemma-dimension-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra, lines 31291-31305), via Tag 00QF (lemma-dimension-inequality-quasi-finite) and Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space)

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q\subset T$ be any prime and let $\mathfrak p$ be its contraction to $P=k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$. Quasi-finiteness at $\mathfrak q$ and the finite-type hypothesis allow [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-inequality-quasi-finite] to be applied, giving $\dim T_{\mathfrak q}\le\dim P_{\mathfrak p}$. Choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ containing $\mathfrak p$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal]. Every prime chain below $\mathfrak p$ is also below $\mathfrak m$, so [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime] gives $\dim P_{\mathfrak p}\le\dim P_{\mathfrak m}=n$, the equality being [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-maximal-localization-dimension]. Thus every local ring of $T$ has dimension at most $n$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00QG (lemma-dimension-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra, lines 31291-31305), via Tags 00QF and 00OP

proof.text: A chain of irreducible closed subsets of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ corresponds, with reversed inclusions, to a chain $\mathfrak q_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak q_r$ of primes of $T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes]. It ends at $\mathfrak q_r$, so [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime] bounds its length $r$ by $\dim T_{\mathfrak q_r}\le n$ from Step 1. Taking the supremum over chains gives $\dim\operatorname{Spec}T\le n$ by [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; if the spectrum is empty this dimension is $-\infty$ by the same definition.
